briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's Cannabis Industry Buckles Under Tax and Oversupply as National Hemp and Psychedelics Fights Intensify
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale cannabis tax and a flower glut are squeezing operators — a Upper Peninsula chain is closing more than half its stores even as the state Supreme Court keeps the tax's legality under review and lawmakers weigh new hemp and psilocybin bills. Nationally, Massachusetts voters head toward a November fight over repealing legal weed, Ohio's hemp market stays split by a narrow federal injunction, and psychedelics drew fresh momentum from Compass Pathways' fast-tracked FDA review and Eli Lilly's multibillion-dollar bet on AtaiBeckley.

local.text: Higher Love closes five of nine Upper Peninsula dispensaries — The retailer is suspending operations at more than half its Michigan locations, blaming the state's new 24% wholesale cannabis tax and collapsing flower prices for the shutdowns.

Michigan Supreme Court keeps 24% wholesale tax fight alive — The Court ordered the state Court of Appeals to expedite its review of whether the tax, passed without a supermajority, illegally amends the 2018 legalization ballot initiative.

CRA releases latest disciplinary action report — The Cannabis Regulatory Agency published its monthly report on licensee violations along with a new tally of denied applications and non-renewed licenses statewide.

Senate bills would move hemp oversight to the CRA — A package including SB 602 would build a state regulatory framework for consumable hemp products and place supervision under the Cannabis Regulatory Agency, still pending in the Legislature.

Psilocybin-for-PTSD bill awaits committee action — State Rep. Mike McFall's bill would shield Michigan adults 18 and older with a PTSD diagnosis from prosecution for possessing up to two ounces of psilocybin, and remains before the House Families and Veterans Committee.

national.text: Warren and Markey oppose Massachusetts repeal measure — Both senators told Marijuana Moment they'll vote no on the November ballot question seeking to roll back the state's 2016 recreational marijuana legalization law.

IRS names cannabis tax guidance a 2026-2027 priority — Treasury and the IRS added Section 280E guidance to their Priority Guidance Plan after House Democrats pushed for clarity on how rescheduling affects marijuana businesses' tax treatment, though formal guidance has yet to be issued.

Federal judge keeps Ohio hemp injunction narrow — U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Helmick's preliminary injunction lets just ten named hemp companies keep selling intoxicating hemp products while Ohio's new in-state cultivation requirement is litigated; the state's attorney general is seeking a stay.

Compass Pathways gets rolling FDA review for psilocybin — The company's COMP360 program was granted a rolling New Drug Application review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher, with full submission still on track for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Eli Lilly buys into psychedelics with AtaiBeckley deal — The pharmaceutical giant agreed to acquire the psychedelics biotech for up to $3.8 billion, including $2.8 billion upfront, gaining an intranasal 5-MeO-DMT depression therapy headed into Phase 3 trials.
